task.title: Bound task field sizes and object reads
task.description:
Nothing limits how large a task document can be, and nothing limits how much of one Workbook will read into memory, so one collaborator can exhaust memory in every clone.

No field limits: NormalizeTask (internal/core/task.go:160-190) trims the title and checks that it is non-blank, and otherwise accepts arbitrary bytes in title, description, and labels. There is no maximum length on any field anywhere in internal/core.

No read limits: readBatchObject parses the object size from the git cat-file --batch header and allocates it unconditionally with make([]byte, int(size)) (internal/gitstore/batch.go:240-247). The whole batch stdout is buffered first, through runGitWithEnvResult which collects into a bytes.Buffer with no cap (internal/gitstore/repository.go:242-252). The non-batch path has the same shape at internal/gitstore/read.go:302-309. Because List batches all task tips into one buffer, the cost is additive across tasks rather than bounded per task.

A collaborator can create a task with a multi-gigabyte description through the ordinary API, since nothing rejects it, or push a hand-built object directly. Every clone that runs fetch, sync, or any auto-syncing mutation then reads it fully into memory.

The web board has the matching gap on its own input side: decodeRequest feeds request.Body to json.Decoder with no http.MaxBytesReader (internal/webui/handler.go:678-691), so a local client can post an arbitrarily large JSON value, and webui.Serve constructs http.Server{Handler: handler} with no ReadHeaderTimeout, ReadTimeout, WriteTimeout, or IdleTimeout (internal/webui/server.go:12), so a stalled connection holds a goroutine and a file descriptor until process exit.

Acceptance:
- NormalizeTask enforces documented maximum lengths on title, description, and label, and on label count, with a clear validation error.
- readBatchObject rejects an object larger than a documented ceiling with CategoryCorruptData rather than allocating it.
- The same ceiling applies on the non-batch read path.
- Mutating web routes wrap the body in http.MaxBytesReader.
- webui.Serve sets ReadHeaderTimeout and IdleTimeout at minimum.
- Tests cover an oversized field rejected on write and an oversized object rejected on read.
- The limits are documented in README so a team knows what a task may hold.
